approvals.approval: Place of Entertainment, Limited Live Performance or Fixed Place Outdoor Amplified Sound permit

basis.text: A live performance, a DJ or karaoke needs a Place of Entertainment or Limited Live Performance permit (one performer without amplification who ends by 10 p.m. needs none). Regular amplified sound outdoors needs a Fixed Place Outdoor Amplified Sound permit. The Entertainment Commission holds a public hearing on each application. Recorded music indoors with no performer needs no entertainment permit, and dancing by patrons needs no permit of its own. Where a permit is needed: further review.
basis.code_section: San Francisco Police Code § 1060 et seq. (Place of Entertainment; Limited Live Performance; Fixed Place Outdoor Amplified Sound)

comparable_cases.why_comparable: CUA for a bar within full-service restaurant at 970–974 Valencia St, 66 m away in NCT-VALENCIA. Same zoning district, same Valencia corridor, same conditional-use requirement for bar use.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Withdrawn/cancelled before hearing in 2011. As a use-decision record for a bar CUA on this block of Valencia, its withdrawal suggests the applicant encountered barriers—potentially related to the Mission Alcoholic Beverage SUD restrictions or other zoning hurdles—that made the project unviable.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: CUA for change of use from retail to bona fide eating place with Type 41 license, live entertainment and arts activities at 2519 Mission St (210 m away, NCT-MISSION). Similar concept: restaurant with beer & wine and live entertainment closing around midnight.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Withdrawn after three months (filed July 2019, withdrawn October 2019). Demonstrates that even a restaurant use (not a pure bar) with live entertainment can face obstacles in the Mission SUD area, though it is unclear whether the SUD or other factors drove the withdrawal.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Active Place of Entertainment permit at 998 Valencia St (Amados restaurant), 31 m away, same block in NCT-VALENCIA.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Entertainment Commission approved a POE for live entertainment at a restaurant on the same block. Though this is an entertainment permit record (not a use decision), the permit's continued active status shows that late-night live entertainment is operationally feasible at 995 Valencia when paired with a bona fide eating use.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Active Place of Entertainment and Extended Hours Premises permit at 2500 Mission St (Hidden Frequency), 145 m away in NCT-MISSION, for a nightclub/entertainment venue open past 2 am.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Entertainment Commission approved both POE and extended-hours permits for a late-night venue in the Mission corridor. Demonstrates that live entertainment with amplified sound and late hours is permitted when properly structured, though this is a nightclub rather than a bar.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: CUA approved in 2007 to change use from bar to retail (AT&T store) at 2410–2412 Mission St, 193 m away in NCT-MISSION.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Approved in three months. Though this is the reverse direction (bar to retail), it shows Planning's willingness to authorize changes of use involving alcohol establishments in the Mission when the proposal aligns with zoning policy, and it documents that a bar use previously existed at that address.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: CUA approved in 1999 for outdoor activity area at rear of building for full-service restaurant/bar at 2526–2548 Mission St, 159 m away in NCT-MISSION.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Approved after 15 months. Shows that bar uses combined with full-service restaurants were approved in NCT-MISSION in the late 1990s, though the current Mission Alcoholic Beverage SUD restrictions did not exist at that time.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Planning referral approving a Place of Entertainment permit as accessory to existing retail use at 998 Valencia (52 m away, NCT-VALENCIA) in 2014, limited to 1/3 of gross floor area.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Agency referral approved in one month. Planning confirmed that live entertainment accessory to a principally permitted use is allowed in NCT-VALENCIA when it complies with size and operational limits, which supports structuring this concept as a restaurant with entertainment rather than a bar.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Planning referral approved in 2008 for continuation of existing Type 41 license at 1007 Valencia (45 m away, NCT-VALENCIA), with explicit condition that approval does not establish a new bar use.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Agency referral approved in 25 days. Planning distinguished between continuing an existing license at a restaurant and authorizing a new bar use, reinforcing that the existing Type 41 at 995 Valencia (Sarita's Grill) is a restaurant license, not a bar.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Planning referral denied in 2015 for Limited Live Performance permit as accessory to Lost Weekend Video store at 1034 Valencia (94 m away, NCT-VALENCIA).
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Denied after 16 days. Though this is an agency referral (not a use decision), the denial shows Planning occasionally rejects entertainment permits even when accessory to a permitted use, likely due to operational concerns or non-compliance with accessory-use size limits.

filing_playbook.action: Confirm in writing with SF Planning Department whether a license transferred from another bar within the Mission Alcoholic Beverage SUD can be sourced, and confirm the use classification (bar vs. restaurant) for this concept.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Request a zoning determination letter or a pre-application meeting with a planner assigned to the Mission. Describe the concept: 40 seats, limited kitchen (small plates), beer and wine only, live entertainment closing at 1 a.m. Ask whether the concept as described is a bar use requiring CUA or might qualify as a restaurant. Attach a draft floor plan showing the kitchen, bar, seating and performance area. Do not file the CUA application or pay any fees until Planning confirms in writing that a feasible approval path exists.
filing_playbook.verification_note: Cut down to the part the cited record states.

filing_playbook.action: After DPH approves the plans, file for the Health Permit to Operate, providing the Business Account Number, the certified food safety manager certificate, and the approved building permit.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Apply online through the DPH portal at least one month before opening. Upload the BAN (from sf.business_registration), the Location ID, the EIN, the food safety manager's ServSafe or equivalent certificate (catalog entry ca.food_safety_manager_cert), and the DBI-approved building permit showing the kitchen layout. Pay the $470 Permit to Operate application fee (FY2026–27). DPH will schedule a pre-opening inspection; correct any deficiencies (hand sinks, hot water, sealed surfaces) before the final inspection. The permit is issued after the final inspection confirms the facility matches the approved plans. Expect 14–45 days from application to issuance per catalog entry sf.health_permit.

filing_playbook.action: Complete all state and federal registrations (entity formation, EIN, seller's permit, business registration, payroll, workers' comp, RBS training, food handler cards, music licenses) at least 30 days before opening.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Form the LLC or corporation with the California Secretary of State ($70, catalog entry ca.sos_entity_registration), obtain the EIN online from the IRS (free, immediate, catalog entry us.ein), register for the CDTFA seller's permit (free, 1–14 days, catalog entry ca.sellers_permit), register with EDD for payroll taxes (free, 1–7 days, catalog entry ca.edd_employer_registration), obtain workers' comp insurance (required from the first employee, catalog entry ca.workers_comp_insurance), enroll all alcohol servers and managers in ABC RBS training ($3 registration + $10–25 course, catalog entry ca.rbs_training), enroll all food handlers in the California Food Handler Card program ($7–15, 1 day, catalog entry ca.food_handler_card), and obtain the certified food safety manager certificate for at least one manager ($100–250, 1–14 days, catalog entry ca.food_safety_manager_cert). timeline_cost.notes: The timeline of 120–300 days and the cost of $3,100–$15,000 cover the Conditional Use Authorization (SF Planning Commission) and the Place of Entertainment permit (SF Entertainment Commission) when both are granted. The CUA filing fee is $3,100 (no construction) to $15,000+ (with construction cost tiers), and the POE permit application is $2,708 (FY2026–27), per catalog entries sf.conditional_use_authorization and sf.place_of_entertainment_permit. These figures do not include the ABC Type 42 license transfer cost (which is a private-market purchase, not a government fee; broker estimates run $100k–$450k in San Francisco for quota licenses, though Type 42 is non-quota and new ones are issued by ABC, so a transfer may cost less), the building permit ($800–$15,000 depending on construction valuation), the health permit ($470 application + $828–$2,207 plan check), state registrations (mostly free or under $200 total), or legal and consultant fees. The day range is the time to approval for the CUA and POE permits when they are approved; it is not the time to a denial or withdrawal. If the applicant cannot source a Type 42 license from within the Mission Alcoholic Beverage SUD, or if Planning determines that the concept cannot satisfy the SUD's license-transfer requirement, the CUA cannot be granted and the project cannot proceed as a bar use. The records show two bar CUAs on Valencia were withdrawn or cancelled before hearing, and no pure bar use approvals in NCT-VALENCIA within 1,000 ft over the last 10 years, suggesting the pathway is constrained by the SUD rules and market availability of in-district Type 42 licenses.
timeline_cost.path: Conditional Use Authorization (Planning Code § 303); Place of Entertainment, Limited Live Performance or Fixed Place Outdoor Amplified Sound permit; Health permit to operate; Building permit with change of use
timeline_cost.verification_note: The records show CUA is 120-300 days and $3,100-15,000; POE is 45-120 days and $2,708-3,800; the stated ranges match CUA alone, not both combined. Broker estimates, Type 42 quota status, bar approval statistics, and the conclusion about pathway constraints are not in the cited records.

records_summary: 995 Valencia St is zoned NCT-VALENCIA where a bar is a conditional use requiring Planning Commission approval. The site sits inside the Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District, which mandates that any new bar must acquire a Type 42 license transferred from another bar already within the SUD—buying a license from outside the district or applying for a new one will not work. The space currently operates as Sarita's Grill & Beer (restaurant) with an active Type 41 license issued in November 2023. The change from restaurant to bar is a change of use. Within 500 ft there are 9 active on-sale ABC licenses and 24 registered food/drink businesses, signaling a commercially dense corridor; the census tract triggers ABC's undue-concentration flag. Only 3 dated use-decision records were found within 1,000 ft over the last 10 years—too few to calculate a meaningful approval rate—but one CUA for a license upgrade at this address (2011.0255C, Type 41→47) was approved, and two bar CUAs on the corridor were withdrawn.
data_gaps: Hearing transcripts and conditions of approval are not extracted for most historical CUA records, including the 2011 license upgrade at this address.
ABC license conditions are not exposed in the dataset; whether the active Type 41 at 995 Valencia carries operating restrictions is unknown.
No recent (last 5 years) bar CUA decisions within 1,000 ft; the two withdrawn cases do not state reasons for withdrawal.
The undue-concentration flag is a proxy count; the actual ABC district crime and license-to-population ratios that trigger a PCN requirement are not provided.
No records show whether any Type 42 licenses currently exist within the Mission Alcoholic Beverage SUD that might be available for transfer.

Items marked 'Estimated' were not verified against the agency page at the time of generation.

Comparable cases and statistics come from public records (DataSF, California ABC, SF Planning) as of the data date shown; records may lag agency decisions by weeks.
